absent: Real peer DMA implementation when the feature is enabled, including provider lifetime and updater semantics.
Contents of power name table and reset method table and their synchronization.
Lock ordering among product data mutex, capability spinlock and MSI lock.
Enumeration and probing logic that populates device, bus and slot fields.
Operational semantics of MSI, MSI-X, ATS, PRI, PASID, DOE, IDE and TSM beyond static offsets.
Hotplug, link power, bandwidth control and error recovery behavior beyond encodings.

findings.text: When peer to peer DMA support is unavailable, managed initialization and resource registration plus provider lookup and multi client queries have inert meanings. Initialization and resource addition signal operation not supported, provider lookup yields absence, multi client distance yields negative one, and multi client memory search yields absence. Supplied device, bar, size, offset, client list, count and verbosity do not change those results.

Peer memory allocation helpers also have inert fallbacks. Device memory allocation and scatter list allocation yield absence, virtual to bus translation yields zero, and release operations plus scatter release plus publication control have no observable effect. Callers may invoke them unconditionally without prior feature checks.

The textual enable control for peer DMA has fixed disabled behavior in the fallback. Storing any input clears the use flag and reports success, while showing state always renders the word none followed by newline. The stored device pointer does not influence either outcome.
Classification of peer mapping support for a given provider and consumer device is fixed to the not supported value in the fallback. No provider state or device property changes the outcome.

Single client convenience wrappers reduce to their multi client counterparts with a unit count. Distance for one provider and one client forwards to the many variant, and memory search for one client forwards similarly. Verbosity passes through unchanged.

Mapping progress for peer transactions is tracked in a small record holding a provider handle and a mapping classification. The provider handle identifies the memory owner and the classification records the outcome of the mapping decision.

State evaluation for a page is gated by build configuration and page kind. If the feature is enabled and the page belongs to peer memory, an external updater refreshes the tracking record and the stored classification is returned. Otherwise the result is the none classification and the record is left untouched.

Conversion from CPU visible physical address to bus address for a peer provider is an offset addition. The provider carries a bus offset bias that is added to the supplied address to obtain the mapped result.

Status error aggregation combines six distinct error conditions covering parity detection, system error signaling, master abort reception, target abort reception, target abort signaling, and general parity. Presence of any member implies presence of the aggregate.

Reset handling uses eight ordered method slots. Probing for reset capability is represented by logical true while performing an actual reset is represented by logical false in the associated boolean control.

Device identification packs bus number in the upper byte and function encoded device number in the lower byte using an eight bit shift and combination. Extraction of the bus number shifts right by eight and keeps only the low byte.

Two slot number sentinels are reserved outside normal numbering. The value selecting all devices is decimal 65023 and the placeholder value is decimal 65535, corresponding to hexadecimal feff and ffff forms.

A physical slot object links its parent bus, participates in a global slot list, optionally references hotplug management, stores a numeric identifier that may hold the all devices sentinel, carries a single bit flag allowing per function slots, and embeds a kernel object for lifetime and naming.
Slot naming exposes the name held by the embedded kernel object through an external helper owned outside this dossier. The helper result is returned directly without additional transformation.
Memory mapping mode for PCI resources distinguishes two states, one for port IO space and one for memory space. The two values are ordered with IO first and memory second.

Resource indexing reserves initial entries for standard base address resources, followed by an expansion ROM entry, optionally followed by virtualization resources when enabled, followed by bridge window resources. Peer bridge windows number three and generic bridge windows number four, with distinct offsets for IO, memory, prefetchable memory, and for CardBus pairs. Total counts and a device resource count alias derive from those bases.
Legacy interrupt signaling uses four lines plus an unknown value. The unknown comes first, followed by four ordered line identifiers. The count of legacy lines is fixed at four.

Configuration read failure is signaled by an all ones value across the full unsigned width. Storing the failure pattern preserves the destination type, and testing for possible failure compares against the same pattern after converting it to the operand type.

Device power is a distinct bitwise integer type with seven named values. Active state is zero, two intermediate low power states are one and two, two off variants are three and four, unknown is five, and error is negative one.
Power state naming resolves through a table lookup that tolerates the negative error value by shifting the index by one before dereferencing. Valid states map to readable names held elsewhere.
IO channel connectivity has three ordered states. Normal operation is one, frozen blocked IO is two, and permanent failure is three. The underlying type is a distinct bitwise unsigned integer.

Express reset control has three ordered commands. Deasserting reset is one, warm reset using platform reset signaling is two, and hot reset using link signaling is three. The type is a distinct bitwise unsigned integer.

Device quirks and capabilities are single bit flags within a distinct bitwise short type. Bits cover virtual manager assignment, translation root marking, bridge alias forcing and suppression, access control quirk state, low power prohibition, bus plus power plus function reset prohibitions, MSI masking presence and legacy disable interaction with MSI-X ordering, product data referral to function zero, and relaxed ordering prohibition. One intermediate position remains unused.

Bus level restrictions are single bit flags with values one, two, four and eight covering MSI prohibition, block write prohibition, error reporting identifier prohibition, and extended configuration prohibition. Interrupt rerouting variants start at one for a specific vendor with a maximum count of three.

Link width encoding uses zero for reserved, an all ones byte for unknown, and lane counts of one, two, four, eight, twelve, sixteen and thirty two. The twelve lane value is the only non power of two member.

Low speed codes cover conventional PCI and PCIX. Code zero means 33 megahertz PCI, code one means 66 megahertz PCI, codes two through four mean PCIX at 66 and 100 and 133 megahertz, codes five through seven repeat those three with error correction, codes nine through eleven repeat them for 266 mode, and codes seventeen through nineteen repeat them for 533 mode.

Higher speed codes cover accelerated graphics and Express generations plus an unknown sentinel. Codes twelve through sixteen span unknown graphics then one, two, four and eight times modes, codes twenty through twenty five span 2.5 through 64 gigatransfers, and code 255 means unknown speed.

Vital product data access state bundles a mutual exclusion lock with a length and a capability offset. The lock serializes access, the length bounds valid data, and the offset locates the capability in configuration space.

Three locking disciplines appear. The product data lock is a sleeping mutex guarding VPD access, the capability lock is a spinlock guarding read modify write cycles to Express capability registers, and the MSI lock is a raw spinlock guarding MSI state including the MSI-X mapping base when that option is present.

A PCI device object anchors topology and identity. It links into its bus list, points to its parent bus and optionally to a subordinate bridged bus and physical slot, carries system private data and proc entries, stores encoded function number plus vendor and device plus subsystem pair plus class triple plus revision plus header type, holds interrupt pin and line, an array of device resources plus a driver exclusive range, physical ROM address and length when not via base address, and embeds a generic device for driver model integration.

The same device object tracks power, errors and capability locations. It records current power state with support and permission bits for low power variants and delays for transitions from off states, error connectivity state, configuration space size, DMA masks and parameters, cached offsets for power management and Express plus MSI plus MSI-X plus link bandwidth plus resizable BAR plus access control plus supported speeds, link power state when enabled, and saved configuration plus capability state for suspend.

Remaining device state covers feature enablement, boolean attributes and optional subsystems. Single bit attributes record bus mastering, MSI status, address translation and related services, virtual function roles, hotplug and enclosure roles, trust and facing, mapping quirks and probing progress, plus private flags and wake signaling. Reset preferences occupy an eight entry ordered array. Conditional members add virtualization linkage, error reporting, complex endpoints, precision time, port containment, object exchange, enclosure management, integrity encryption with stream allocators, and telemetry state.

Physical function resolution returns the associated physical device when the queried device is a virtual function and virtualization support is present, otherwise it returns the input unchanged. Channel liveness is false exactly when stored error state differs from normal operation.

Conversion from generic device to PCI device uses container embedding. Iteration helpers walk all devices forward or in reverse by repeatedly querying for any vendor and device identifier until exhaustion.

Several hazards follow from the definitions. Fallback peer paths silently disable acceleration by returning absence or not supported, all ones configuration data is ambiguous between genuine content and read failure, any non normal channel state must be treated as offline, devices flagged untrusted or external facing may issue hostile direct memory access, and reset plus power plus mapping quirk flags forbid operations that would otherwise appear legal.
